analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/sandbox-setup-resize.md) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The doc describes `darkbloom sandbox setup` on an already-set-up Mac re-running the add-on installer with `--plan` (read-only). When the plan's slot counts differ from the installed ones, setup asks the user to apply the plan. With `--yes` or without a TTY, it applies only when the plan adds slots and removes none. The docs also say exit 4 (job running) is surfaced and that the CLI never passes the installer's `--force`.

Security relevance (TB-013 / T-061 / A-019): the described flow reuses the existing download-and-run-installer path. The docs state no new privilege, endpoint or trust change. The non-interactive apply is bounded to additive plans, and the documentation says jobs are never force-stopped. This is a conservative design as described. No real code is in this batch, so the actual implementation (SandboxSlotChange, SandboxSizingPlan.freeSpaceNote, plan JSON parsing, the installer invocation and the `--yes` path) is unverified. A later source pass should check these points:
- The plan's `linux_slots`/`macos_slots` values are validated and bounded before being passed as `--linux-slots`/`--macos-slots`.
- The installer's output is not trusted for command-line construction.
- The printed fallback command is shell-safe.
- `--force` is truly never passed.

The free-space note and the tmutil guidance are informational only. Nothing here touches TB-012 (hold socket), the attestation/App Attest boundaries, or the T-041 prefix-cache definition provided as context. No threat-model assumption is invalidated and no new attack surface is evident from the docs alone. Whether the non-interactive apply in the real code stays within the documented additive-only limit is not verifiable from this batch.
